Astro's new tab is astro-newtab (REPLACE, #22) and its tiles are ntp-tiles (REPLACE, #22), so the scheme has no consumer here — and what it carries is a security relaxation, not a feature. chrome-search://most-visited is exempted from the WebUI process lock (chrome_content_browser_client.cc:2001-2017), and that exemption is consumed twice: child_process_security_policy_impl.cc:1523-1534 skips the lock check outright for an exempt WebUI URL, and :281-294 (AllowProcessLockMismatchForNTP) tolerates a lock mismatch. | `webui-host-namespace` | PRESENT | **REPLACE** | #10 | `none` | The rule: no Astro-owned WebUI data source may register under a host name that Chromium's ChromeURLHosts() (chrome/common/webui_url_constants.cc:75-242) contains. Adopting it is what turns this from a blocker on most of #10 into a naming constraint — #11 does not need to know WHICH chrome:// hosts survive if no astro:// host name is a chrome:// host name, and that holds at any point in #10's lifetime. It is strictly stronger than the question it replaces, not weaker. Where Astro reuses a Chromium page rather than registering its own source there is no collision and no rename, because there is only one registration; the rule constrains Astro-OWNED sources. The two colliding names are recorded as `webui_host: not-determined` on their entries, because whether astro-settings renames or reuses Chromium Settings is #15's call and whats-new is #14's. |
| `webui-scheme-trust-split` | NOT_BUILT | **REPLACE** | #10 | `none` | The split is not a style choice, it is forced by the loader. A document holding WebUI bindings has its network factory revoked (render_frame_host_impl.cc:12645-12657), so the rule is: a page whose own JavaScript must reach the network cannot be bound, and therefore lives on astro-untrusted://; every other page is bound and lives on astro://. Applying that rule to the manifest's own `network` column gives the per-page assignment, recorded as `scheme_trust` on each page entry: alia is untrusted (its panel calls api.alia.onl from the page); astro-newtab, astro-settings, astro-whats-new, astro-error-page, astro-adblock-webui and first-run-page are trusted (their endpoints are either `none` or user-initiated link navigations away from the page, not requests the page makes). The untrusted scheme's registration rows, decided: cors_enabled YES (mirroring url_schemes.cc:93 — without it a cross-origin API call from the untrusted page is not even reachable), secure YES for both schemes (:71-74; otherwise neither is a secure context), service_worker NO for both (Chrome pushes both at :120-121 but the renderer only honours it behind features::kEnableServiceWorkersForChromeScheme / kEnableServiceWorkersForChromeUntrusted, render_thread_impl.cc:824-827, :834-838; no Astro page needs one and a service worker is persistent code on a privileged-adjacent origin), savable NO for both (page-saving-savable-schemes), and no_access / local / csp_bypassing / empty_document NO for both. |

## Decisions that block another issue

| Feature | Blocks | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `chrome-search-scheme` | #11 | #11 writes AstroContentBrowserClient::GetAdditionalWebUISchemes, and that function's return value IS the WebUI scheme set (url_data_manager_backend.cc:63-67). The list is memoised into a process-lifetime NoDestructor (:70-84, read at :282-288) and url::LockSchemeRegistries() closes the URL registry (content/common/url_schemes.cc:128-129), so neither this row nor the process-lock exemption it drags in is revocable at runtime — changing it later is a code change plus a restart. #11 has to know whether the scheme survives before it writes the function. |
| `dom-distiller-scheme` | #11 | Same mechanism as chrome-search-scheme: it is a row of GetAdditionalWebUISchemes, memoised for the process lifetime (url_data_manager_backend.cc:70-84) behind a locked URL registry (content/common/url_schemes.cc:128-129). It blocks #11's Android build only — #11's desktop milestone 1 can proceed on the measured desktop half, which is that the scheme has no entry point there. Recorded as a blocker rather than guessed, because the wrong guess is unfixable without a rebuild. |
| `oxy-identity` | #11 | May a remote origin reach the trusted scheme? Decided: NO, and the scheme must not ship an auth host until the mechanism exists to enforce it. Measured: Chromium's guard against a web redirect chain landing on a privileged URL is content::IsSafeRedirectTarget (content/public/common/url_utils.cc:81-107), which rejects a target via HasWebUIScheme at :95 — and HasWebUIScheme reads a three-element literal, {chrome, chrome-untrusted, devtools}, at :27-31. That literal is in //content/public/common, has no ContentBrowserClient extension point (the renderer has none), and `astro` is not in it, nor in the function's kUnsafeSchemes set at :82-94. So IsSafeRedirectTarget returns TRUE for an https:// -> astro:// redirect and content/browser/loader/navigation_url_loader_impl.cc:1575-1577 does not raise net::ERR_UNSAFE_REDIRECT. Any HTTPS site — not merely auth.oxy.so — could 302 a top-level navigation to astro://auth/callback?access_token=<attacker's>, against a handler that reads credentials out of its own query string (src/chrome/browser/oxy/oxy_auth_service.h:22-23, oxy_auth_callback_handler.h:15): session fixation straight into the browser's identity store. Consequences for #11, in order: (a) milestone 1 registers the schemes with a diagnostic host and NO auth host, which needs nothing from #16; (b) no host that consumes a credential may ship on astro:// until IsWebUIScheme is generalised into a common-layer scheme store; (c) #16 rebuilds the flow on Authorization Code + PKCE so no token rides a URL, which removes the payload but not the redirect reachability — both are needed. What is NOT decided here is #16's identity architecture; only the scheme-transport bit is. |
| `page-saving-savable-schemes` | #11 | savable_schemes is a ContentClient::Schemes row, assigned once in RegisterContentSchemes behind the g_registered_url_schemes early return (content/common/url_schemes.cc:54-57, :131-136), so it is a startup-time decision like every other row. Without this bit answered, #11 ships a scheme descriptor asserting `not savable` whose enforcement path has been stubbed to `return true` — a registry stating something false about the product, which is the exact failure #10's separation of `state` from `observed_state` exists to prevent. |
| `webui-host-namespace` | #11 | #11 deletes the astro://-to-chrome:// alias, and the moment it does, `settings` and `whats-new` become two pages sharing one map key. The winner is whichever of chrome://settings and astro://settings the user opened last in that profile, because the source is added when the controller is constructed; the loser returns net::ERR_INVALID_URL. Order-dependent, per-profile, per-session, silent. #11 needs the rule before it removes the alias — not the full list of surviving chrome:// hosts, which is the point of adopting a rule instead. |
| `webui-scheme-trust-split` | #11 | Two reasons, both registration-time. First, the untrusted scheme's rows — CORS, service workers, secure, savable — are ContentClient::Schemes vectors applied once in RegisterContentSchemes and then sealed by url::LockSchemeRegistries() (content/common/url_schemes.cc:59, :92-95, :120-121, :128-129), so they cannot be decided after the fact, and they cannot be decided at all without knowing what the untrusted scheme is FOR. Second, a page assumed trusted and later found to need the network has three exits and all three are bad: move it to the untrusted scheme (a different origin, so persisted URLs, bookmarks and session entries break), add it to an Astro copy of IsWebUIAllowedToMakeNetworkRequests (re-creating crbug.com/829412's debt on day one), or ship a privileged page with a network loader. |
| `astro-internal-schemes` | #12, #13, #14 | Everything downstream of the scheme depends on this decision being taken first, which is why the epic orders #11 -> #12 -> #13. #14 is on the same side of the arrow and was previously encoded backwards: what a trusted astro:// document may execute is part of the scheme's trust model, so #11 fixes the floor before #14 packages pages onto it (see webui-csp-and-trusted-types, whose own blocks_reason already said so). |
| `webui-fonts` | #14 | The remote font provider is #14's to remove when it packages the WebUI resources. |

## Internal page inventory

Which of the two internal schemes each page lands on, and the bare host its data source registers under. `scheme_trust` is not a preference: a document holding WebUI bindings has its network factory revoked, so a page whose own JavaScript must reach the network cannot be bound and therefore cannot be trusted. The rules that produce these two columns are `webui-scheme-trust-split` and `webui-host-namespace`.

| Feature | Scheme | Host | Endpoints the page reaches | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `astro-adblock-webui` | **trusted** | `adblock` | `none` | #18 |
| `astro-error-page` | **trusted** | `astro-error` | `none` | #14 |
| `astro-newtab` | **trusted** | `astro-ntp` | `none` | #22 |
| `astro-settings` | **trusted** | `not-determined` | `none` | #15 |
| `astro-whats-new` | **trusted** | `not-determined` | `none` | #14 |
| `first-run-page` | **trusted** | `not-determined` | `first-run-chromium-source`, `first-run-wiki` | #24 |
| `alia` | **untrusted** | `alia` | `alia-api` | #17 |

What #11 reads here is a trap, not a decision: content/public/browser/url_data_source.cc:19-28 decides the untrusted CSP branch by testing whether the SOURCE NAME starts with `chrome-untrusted://`, so an astro:// or astro-untrusted:// source takes the trusted branch of every directive — script-src naming chrome://resources (:74-79) and an EMPTY default-src (:69-71) where chrome-untrusted would get `default-src 'self'`. The script-src half is self-punishing: the subresource factory is scheme-bound and calls mojo::ReportBadMessage("Incorrect scheme") on anything else (content/browser/webui/web_ui_url_loader_factory.cc:284-299), so the default CSP grants an astro:// page a scheme its own loader kills it for using. Upstream's answer is a per-scheme resources host (url_data_manager_backend.cc:87-99 registers both chrome://resources and chrome-untrusted://resources); Astro must do the same or override the directives. |
| `webui-fonts` | #11 | REPLACE means self-hosted WOFF2, so no Astro page fetches a font. #11 reads that as one input to the per-page network posture in webui-scheme-trust-split: it is why the six trusted pages can be trusted at all. It is not a decision #11 waits on — it is already taken. |
